highlight.text: But I have made a series of colour studies in painting, simply flowers, red poppies, blue corn flowers and myosotys, white and rose roses, yellow chrysanthemums-seeking oppositions of blue with orange, red and green, yellow and violet

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 459a to Horace M. Livens, Paris, August–October 1886
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

highlight.lead: Van Gogh describing his Paris experiments:

work.text: In these works, he simplified his palette, employed more vibrant colors, and used a thicker, broader paint application than he had earlier. Here he explored the use of complementary colors—yellow and purple, blue and orange, and red and green—in the service of chromatic intensity.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: Collection description: Grapes, Lemons, Pears, and Apples

moment.text: The painting was probably among the “violent still lifes”—to quote Van Gogh’s friend the painter Emile Bernard—that he included in the group exhibition of young avant-garde artists that he organized at a local restaurant in November–December 1887.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: Collection description: Grapes, Lemons, Pears, and Apples

matters.text: So as we said at the time: in colour seeking life the true drawing is modelling with colour. I did a dozen landscapes too, frankly green frankly blue. And so I am struggling for life and progress in art.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 459a to Horace M. Livens, Paris, August–October 1886
